classification.difficultyReason: Extend the partial tree while stopping paths when either player reaches two wins, then identify and combine terminal paths of different lengths for a series win and a three-game series.

content.prompt: Xena and Gabrielle compete in a series of games. The series finishes when one player has won two games. In any game, the probability that Xena wins is $\frac{2}{3}$ and the probability that Gabrielle wins is $\frac{1}{3}$. Part of the tree diagram for this series of games is shown.

spec.description: Only the two black supplied branches and their probabilities; the blue completion is excluded from the student diagram.
spec.mathematics: Upper branch has probability 2/3; lower branch has probability 1/3.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent student-visible partial tree; no supplied response labels.

children.prompt: Complete the tree diagram, showing the possible outcomes (there are only 6).

answer.worked: Use $X$ for a Xena win and $G$ for a Gabrielle win. At every continuing stage, label the $X$ branch $\frac{2}{3}$ and the $G$ branch $\frac{1}{3}$. Stop the $XX$ and $GG$ paths after the second game. Continue only $XG$ and $GX$ to a third game. The six terminal outcomes are $XX$, $XGX$, $XGG$, $GXX$, $GXG$ and $GG$.

spec.description: Complete three-stage tree with six terminal paths. Preserve the N/A third-game entries for XX and GG; make both terminating outcome strings explicit. Ordinary strokes and labels use house black.
spec.mathematics: X branches have probability 2/3 and G branches 1/3. XX and GG stop after two games; XG and GX branch once more. Terminal outcomes are XX, XGX, XGG, GXX, GXG, GG.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; excluded from the student prompt.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the probability Gabrielle wins the series?

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the probability three games are played in the series?

answer.worked:
The series ends after two games only on $XX$ or $GG$.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{three games})&=1-\bigl(P(XX)+P(GG)\bigr)\\&=1-\left(\frac{2}{3}\times\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3}\times\frac{1}{3}\right)\\&=1-\left(\frac{4}{9}+\frac{1}{9}\right)\\&=\frac{4}{9}\end{align*}$$
